body.instructions: CONTEXT: Two speech-recognition versions, version_A and version_B, transcribed the same short span of an outpatient consultation. Which engine made which is hidden. Lines look like [mm:ss] ROLE: native text [EN: English gloss]. Numbers, doses and dates are compared in code. QUESTION: Which version is the more faithful transcript of what was said? RULES: Prefer the version a clinician could rely on. Do not prefer a version for length or fluency alone.

criteria.version_A: Version A is clearly the more faithful.
criteria.version_B: Version B is clearly the more faithful.

body.instructions: CONTEXT: Two speech-recognition versions, version_A and version_B, transcribed the same short span of an outpatient consultation. Which engine made which is hidden. Lines look like [mm:ss] ROLE: native text [EN: English gloss]. Numbers, doses and dates are compared in code. QUESTION: Do the two versions differ in clinical meaning? RULES: Spelling-only and homophone differences are not clinical differences. A negation flip changes meaning.

criteria.same_meaning: The two versions mean the same.
criteria.negation_flip: One version negates what the other affirms.
criteria.laterality_or_site: They differ on left or right, or on a body site.
criteria.drug_or_procedure_name: They name a different drug or procedure.
criteria.other_clinical_change: They differ in some other clinically relevant way.
criteria.non_clinical_difference: They differ only in non-clinical wording or spelling.
